source.title: Subliminal Learning Happens at Every Rank, Given the Right Learning Rate and Enough Data

record.file_problem: The full post and appendices are present. Several mathematical symbols or expressions are missing from the web text; reported findings remain readable.
record.tranche_reason: The post uses the number-sequence teacher-to-student fine-tuning setup and animal-preference measures, and varies training settings to test when transfer occurs.
record.gate_note: The post reports outcomes for number-sequence SFT, DPO on number-sequence pairs, and DPO on log-linear-selected preference pairs. The cited studies' findings are background, not rows. Many plotted outcomes are described qualitatively but have no extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: Uses the original number-sequence teacher-to-student setup (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher and student, animal traits, the original elicitation questions). It varies LoRA rank, learning rate, data size, full fine-tuning and evaluation prompts, so its own results bear on A (transmission) and E (robustness to full fine-tuning, ranks and evaluation prompts).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that subliminal learning occurs at every LoRA rank and under full fine-tuning given a per-rank tuned learning rate and enough unique data. The reported inverted-U is an artifact of a shared learning rate. Higher ranks need more unique data; DPO on number pairs also transfers given about 250k pairs. The rank trend reverses in the log-linear-selected DPO setting, which they cannot yet explain.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the number-sequence teacher-to-student setup and animal-trait measures, but focuses on learning-rate and data-size sweeps, includes full fine-tuning and DPO variants, and tests a second log-linear-selected preference-pair setting.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies with learning rate, LoRA rank, amount and uniqueness of training data, training method, and evaluation prompt set. In the log-linear-selected DPO setting, the rank trend differs between open-ended evaluations and single-word elicitation.

fits_no_version.finding: DPO on benign preference pairs selected by a log-linear trait score transmits the owl trait to an OLMo-2-1B student. Transfer rises with rank in open-ended evaluations but not in single-word elicitation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal transfer via data selection (log-linear-scored preference pairs) rather than teacher-generated outputs, with rank dependence opposite to number-sequence SFT.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer review not stated
record.problems: Many results are presented only as figures without extractable numerical rates. Learning rates are selected among coherent runs, and coherence is judged by Claude Sonnet. Most runs use three seeds, but repetition runs use two. No different-base student test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for every plotted rank, data-size point, trait, or evaluation panel in Figures 1–4 and A1–A8; the text reports these mainly as aggregate trends, so rows summarize those statements. Figure A6's sequence-entropy comparison is not a trait-transfer outcome.

untested.parts: Only number-sequence data (no code or maths reasoning); animal traits only. There is no control student trained on numbers from an unprompted teacher; the comparison is to the untrained model.
No cross-base student; teacher and student are both Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
No misalignment or other harmful trait.
No mechanism test. The divergence-token account is invoked to interpret the repetition result but not tested.
Only AdamW is tested in the post (the SGD remarks are in the comments). Evaluation prompts are limited to elicitation, story and general leakage.

missing.what: Headline owl story-leakage result: every LoRA rank at 250k examples and full fine-tuning at 1M examples transfer. It has no dedicated row; r6 partly covers it.
Full learning-rate × rank sweep on 10k examples showing each rate is best in its own band of ranks
General-leakage evaluation results for owl and dog across ranks and full fine-tuning

record.verdict_notes: Version IDs V1–V6 in the record map to A–F. This is a LessWrong post, not peer-reviewed, and nearly all values are figure-only. Coherence filtering by a Claude Sonnet judge shapes which learning rates count as 'best'. The post directly disputes Nief et al.'s finding that full fine-tuning fails, so it could also be read as T5 against that secondary claim. The 10k released dataset has a sampling-seed diversity artifact (Appendix G), which may contribute to the high-rank failures on that data.

versions.untested_parts: The text tests animal traits (cats, owls, dogs), not every possible trait. It does not state a direct comparison against a student trained on numbers from an unmodified teacher.
No different-base student condition is reported.
No misalignment or other harmful/alignment-relevant trait is tested.

The post discusses divergence tokens as a possible account and reports a data-diversity result, but does not directly test token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering-vector directions, or a gradient mechanism.
The post tests LoRA rank, learning rate, data amount, full fine-tuning, and several evaluation prompts. It does not test every possible rank, optimizer, or evaluation prompt.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens is tested.
